topic.title: DITA Bootstrap AST Plug-in & Publishing
topic.shortdesc: Simple guide on publishing DITA documentation into the React Harness data store, comparing transtypes, and automated CI publishing.

section.title: Plug-in Overview & Installation
section.p: The org.dita-bootstrap.ast plug-in allows authors to publish DITA documentation into the React Harness library. Install the plug-in into your DITA Open Toolkit instance:
section.codeblock: # Install plug-ins using the dita command: dita install fox.jason.extend.css dita install org.dita-bootstrap.ast

section.title: Publishing to the Document Store
section.p: Publishing your documentation set requires a single command:
section.codeblock: # Publish documentation directly into the data store: dita --input=path/to/your.ditamap \ --format=ast-bootstrap \ --output=react-harness/data-store/data/my-doc-set
section.p: Move or save the generated files to the data store directory (data-store/data/my-doc-set)—and that's it! The data store automatically discovers your document set and adds it to your browser library catalog.

plentry.pd: Generates interactive documentation files for the React Harness web reader and AI Assistant chat.
Generates static HTML5 web pages styled with Bootstrap 5.3 for standard web servers.

section.title: Customizing Chrome (Headers & Footers)
section.p: Custom navigation headers and footers can be passed during publishing via command-line options:
Header templates support special interactive roles:

ul.li: document-title/ — Inserts the title of the document set.
role="search" — Renders the header search bar.
role="theme-toggle" — Renders the Light/Dark mode selector.
role="clear-chat" — Renders a clear chat conversation button in the AI Assistant.

section.title: Central Design System (chrome.json)
section.p: The chrome.json file (located at data-store/data/chrome.json) provides fallback header, footer, card, and chat interface templates. If a published document set does not include a custom header, the system automatically uses chrome.json to maintain consistent branding across all document sets.

section.title: Automated CI Publishing to GitHub Pages
section.p: You can automate documentation publishing using GitHub Actions. Add a workflow file at .github/workflows/docs-gh-pages.yml:
section.codeblock:
name: Build and Deploy Documentation to GitHub Pages
on: push: branches: - main - master paths: - 'react-harness/sample/**' - '.github/workflows/docs-gh-pages.yml' workflow_dispatch:
permissions: contents: write
jobs: build-and-deploy-docs: name: Build & Deploy DITA Documentation runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - name: Git Checkout uses: actions/checkout@v4
- name: Build DITA AST Documentation uses: dita-ot/dita-ot-action@master with: install: | dita install fox.jason.extend.css dita install org.dita-bootstrap.html dita install org.dita-bootstrap.ast input: react-harness/sample/document.ditamap transtype: ast-bootstrap output-path: out/sample
- name: Deploy Documentation to GitHub Pages uses: JamesIves/github-pages-deploy-action@v4.6.0 with: token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }} branch: gh-pages folder: out/sample
